course_details.Overview of class: This survey-style course serves as the foundational course for the Farley undergraduate minor in entrepreneurship. It is also a good choice for students who simply wish to familiarize themselves with the world of entrepreneurship. Students will learn to think like entrepreneurs, and will be introduced to key topics relevant to entrepreneurship, including customer discovery, finance, and marketing. They will also learn how to understand and analyze a broad range of entrepreneurial activity, and will have the opportunity to locate their own goals and values within the field of entrepreneurship.

course_details.Overview of class: This course meets a core requirement for the Farley undergraduate minor in entrepreneurship. The goal of the course is to teach students about the tools and strategies that startups use to generate revenue. It covers a broad range of topics related to sales and marketing including branding, positioning, lead generation, direct selling, social media, content marketing, influencer marketing, SEO, paid search, email marketing and other current trends. The class is a mixture of lecture, breakout groups and guest speakers.

course_details.Overview of class:
The process of innovation - developing a new idea, creating a novel product, and scaling production - cannot be accomplished single-handedly. Rather, innovation requires a collaborative team and a leader who can build an organization that is willing and able to share knowledge, resolve differences, and learn together.

This course is designed for undergraduates who want to understand transformational leadership and the unique role that leaders play in nurturing teams to problem-solve, collaborate, and continuously innovate.

We will examine leadership and the impact of leadership styles on team effectiveness, drawing from theories and case studies, as well as our personal experiences. We will explore organizational culture, motivation, conflict management, and communication. Finally, we will develop our own approaches to leadership as we tackle innovation work - whether in the classroom as students or in the industry as future entrepreneurs and executives.

course_details.Overview of class: This survey-style course introduces students to some of the most common ways that entrepreneurs secure funding for new ventures. Students will be exposed to a variety of funding strategies and approaches, including venture capital, crowdfunding, and bootstrapping.

course_details.Topic: Frontlines of Food: The Innovations Reshaping the
course_details.Overview of class: Food innovation is reshaping how we eat, from breakthrough products and technologies to new business models, dining experiences, and creative responses to food system challenges. In this course, students will learn to read emerging trends, identify entrepreneurial opportunities, and build their own perspective on what matters most in today's food landscape. Throughout the quarter, guest speakers will discuss the problems they're tackling, the innovations they're building, and the opportunities they see on the horizon.

NUvention: Medical is designed to expose students to the holistic process of developing and commercializing new medical technologies through the lens of a startup. A partnership between four Northwestern schools, this class brings together students in interdisciplinary teams to simulate the ways in which medical innovations evolve from clinical needs and become viable ventures. Students engage with challenges tied to product development, intellectual property, industry regulations, and business modeling as they learn what it means to be entrepreneurial in the medical technology space. This course spans two quarters, fall 2023 and winter 2024, and satisfies the experiential course requirement for undergraduate and graduate students in the entrepreneurship minor program.

course_details.Overview of class: NUvention: Media & AI brings together students from across Northwestern schools to explore how artificial intelligence and computational technologies will shape the future of media, and who want to learn a process for creating new, AI-powered ventures in the news and media space. Student teams will use human-centered design methods to identify an opportunity gap, design interaction and presentation models, build functioning prototypes that fulfill those needs, and develop a compelling pitch and business plan to launch and sustain their product/service. Along the way, students will learn an innovation and venture development process. Students will interact with industry veterans and domain experts who inspire and guide the student team as they pursue their projects.

This course aims to enable students' entrepreneurial success while challenging them to build the best product they can possibly build by using key insights from entrepreneurs and product managers at successful companies. The course focuses on customer problems, customer research, simple MVP tests, market requirements, product requirements, and product vision decks. By the end of the quarter, students will be well-versed in the fundamentals of product management.

NUvention: Biotechnology responds to the growing demand for innovation in biotechnology by bringing together interdisciplinary student teams from across Northwestern to develop ventures that harness biology to address societal challenges. Focusing on applications in areas including food, agriculture, sustainable materials, energy, consumer products, industrial biotechnology, and diagnostics, students will identify market opportunities, evaluate commercialization pathways, and build new ventures around biotechnology-enabled solutions. The course focuses on biotechnology ventures outside the pharmaceutical and therapeutic sectors and does not cover products requiring FDA drug approval. Developed in partnership with Northwestern's Center for Synthetic Biology, the course introduces students to the unique opportunities and challenges of bringing biotechnology innovations to market.
